banner: Demo. **Ledgerline** is a made-up legacy invoicing app. Every number here is invented to show the report.
summary: Invoices and the API are mapped and guarded by checks. The current bottleneck is PDF rendering. Reports and the old admin are still in the fog.

win.rocket: Invoices, payments and the API reach **assembler** tier, and month-end runs in under 10 minutes.

items.text: Areas in scope at assembler tier

since: Payments moved up to **assembler**: characterization tests pin refunds, and the suite runs in the pre-commit hook. **reports** went stale: 4 files changed since it was checked.

bottleneck.title: PDF rendering runs one invoice at a time
bottleneck.body: Month-end renders every invoice in a single loop and waits for each PDF before starting the next. That loop is about 30 of the 38 minutes.
bottleneck.plan: Pin today's PDFs with byte-for-byte snapshot tests, then render in a small worker pool. Run it as the `month-end-time` hill climb.
bottleneck.evidence: jobs/month_end.php:212 · profile of the 3 Oct run: 31m 40s in render_invoice()

questions.text: Does anyone still use **admin-legacy**, or did the new admin replace all of it?
Must invoice PDFs stay byte-identical, or only look the same?
questions.evidence: Decides how strict the snapshot tests for pdf-render must be.

questions.text: Why does month-end skip invoices created after 23:00 on the last day?
questions.evidence: jobs/month_end.php:88 · no comment, no linked issue

hillclimbs.title: Shorten the month-end run
hillclimbs.why: It blocks finance for most of an hour, and PDF rendering is most of it.
hillclimbs.metric: Wall time of month-end on the 2,000-invoice fixture

hillclimbs.title: Cut queries on the dashboard
hillclimbs.why: The dashboard runs one query per customer. It slows as customers grow.

findings.title: Tax is calculated in two places
findings.body: The invoice screen and the PDF compute tax separately. They round differently on mixed-rate invoices.

findings.title: Dashboard runs one query per customer
findings.body: A loop loads each customer's balance on its own.
findings.evidence: app/Dashboard/Balances.php:61 · 214 queries on the demo data

findings.title: The `utils` file is a junction
findings.body: 38 files import it, and it mixes dates, money and HTML helpers.

findings.title: Import job has no tests
findings.body: It ran last in March. It may be dead.

upgrades.title: Payments: pin refunds with characterization tests
upgrades.note: Tier 1 → 2. The suite runs in the pre-commit hook.

upgrades.title: Cache customer balances for the dashboard
upgrades.note: Inside run-to-run noise. The real cost is the query count.

upgrades.title: API: batch the invoice list query

trends.area: invoices · ratchet added in session 4, baseline only goes down
reports · stale since the tax change, needs a fresh look

ridealongs.title: Split `InvoiceService.send` into render and deliver
ridealongs.improves: Lets e-invoicing add a third delivery channel without touching PDF rendering.
ridealongs.vehicle: E-invoicing (Q1), or any change to invoice delivery

ridealongs.title: Run customer statements in batches of 500
ridealongs.improves: Cuts month-end by about 12 minutes in the replay. Ships behind a flag, off by default.

ridealongs.title: Characterization tests for the tax summary
ridealongs.improves: Pins today's tax totals so the new tax report can change the code safely.
ridealongs.evidence: src/reports/tax.ts:1–240 · needs the area verified again first

stories.title: Why invoices lock at 23:00
stories.body: The old bank export ran at 23:30 and read the invoices table directly. Locking at 23:00 kept totals still while it ran. The export moved to the API in 2023, so the lock may no longer be needed.
stories.source: engineer, session 4 · git blame on month_end.php

stories.title: Two admins
stories.body: The new admin was built beside the old one to avoid a big-bang switch. Finance still uses the old one for credit notes.
